the fence is the builder-aider row's whole point and it was watched to FAIL before it was trusted: with escalation.allow removed the provider became p-cheap, the dial became http://cheap:11434/api/chat, and route_walked lost its stated reason — three assertions red independently, then green twice restored.

THE ROW WAS THE BUILD'S OWN ERROR AND THE PROOF CAUGHT IT: authoring builder-aider turned test_route.py's equality assertion red, and the FIRST reading of that red here was that the assertion had gone stale and should be widened to admit a fourth kind of row. That is the plaster the deterministic-red rule exists to stop, and it got one step from being applied. Akien's ruling, 2026-08-16, verbatim: "no. absolfuckinglutely no. The inference proxy knows about providers and models. it does not understand about consumers. the consumer asks for what it wants. period, end of story." The red was correct and the build was wrong; the equality was RESTORED, not loosened, and the row removed (8 deletions in stacks/domains.json).

THE WHY BENEATH THE RULING, and it is why this cannot recur as a special case — Akien, 2026-08-16, verbatim: "if the inference proxy knows about consumers, then there is no need for domains. and then the inference proxy becomes extremely complicated. That's why this is a no. we already know that when a single component gets very complicated, all levels of claude begin to have trouble". The row is SELF-COLLAPSING: admit one caller-named row and every caller earns one, at which point a vertical stops meaning a shape of ask and starts meaning a class of consumer — the domains stack becomes a consumer registry and there was never a reason to have domains at all. This is falsifier tell 6 from the stack's own authoring ticket ("rows are FIELD SETS an instance composes, never classes it belongs to") tripped by a build that had the sentence in front of it. The second half is a MEASURED cost that generalizes past this proxy: complexity concentrated in one component degrades every tier of Claude working on it.

THE FENCE HAS NO HOLDER RIGHT NOW, and that is stated rather than papered over. The removed row was the only money-fence between the chat verb and a paid provider. Under the ruling the fence belongs to the consumer — the shim asks for hex and qwen3-coder:30b by name, and asking for exactly that IS the safety — but the shim is not built. So between now and the aider-shim build, nothing structural stops a chat request naming an expensive model; the general default and the models stack are all that stand. Carried forward on tickets/aider-shim.json as a build obligation.

THE THREE SURVIVING ROWS WERE EXAMINED FOR THE SAME ERROR AND ARE NOT IT — the check the ruling invites. general/coding/research are named for SHAPES OF ASK, and each composes prompts + walk-rule as field sets. Their why-prose does cite first consumers (research: "the librarian's vertical"; coding: "the vertical the future fail-over-to-LLM inspectors ride") — that is PROVENANCE for why the shape was authored, not a class the caller belongs to. The distinguisher is what a second consumer does: a second research-shaped caller rides `research` unchanged, whereas a second build device could never have ridden `builder-aider`. Flagged for Akien's eye, answered rather than escalated as an open question.

THE VERDICT'S CRITERION 2 CARRIED A MALFORMED INSTRUMENT AND IS CORRECTED HERE RATHER THAN EDITED THERE (Law 7 — the berth stands). As written it said no shipped stack, module OR PROOF may name 'builder-aider'. Akien, 2026-08-16: "why would we say 'no proof may name builder-aider'? how the fuck do we prove the thing itself then?" He is right and the criterion is self-defeating: proving an absence REQUIRES naming the absent thing, so a tooth that reds when the row returns must write the string. The criterion forbade the only proof that would make the property enforceable. THE PROPERTY IS RIGHT AND THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG: what matters is that the shipped stack carries no consumer-named row and no code branches on one, and the instrument for that is the EQUALITY in test_route.py, set(table['rows']) == {'general','coding','research'} — which is strictly stronger than a name-grep because it reds on ANY fourth row, not just the one this build happened to author. A future builder-claude or librarian-shim row trips it identically; the grep would have caught one name and missed the class. AND THE PROCESS FAILURE IS THE SAME REFLEX ONE LAYER UP. On the first pass the temptation was to widen a red assertion to admit what had just been built. On the second, the criterion itself was broken and it was preserved with a paragraph explaining why its literal failure was acceptable ('documentary, not executable'). The paragraph IS the plaster. A malformed criterion is fixed or it carries a ruling — explaining around it is the third disposition that does not exist.
